lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be left off the résumé.
items.because: They do not help assess the qualifications, can introduce irrelevant screening considerations, and use space without strengthening the application.

items.says: The résumé has an unexplained 10-month gap between the B.S. and the Junior Software Engineer role.
items.because: The gap leaves readers unsure what occupied the period from June 2022 to May 2023.

items.says: The 35% diagnostic-accuracy improvement lacks a baseline, endpoint, and evaluation-set context.
items.because: Readers cannot judge the size or credibility of the improvement or distinguish a broad result from a narrow test.

items.says: The phrase "each of 3 specialist agents" uses awkward number styling in a dense sentence.
items.because: The numeral interrupts the technical clause and makes the reader parse the count.

items.says: The grouped-rollout method chain delays the two measurable results in the GRPO bullet.
items.because: Readers must move through several method details before reaching the tool-call and latency reductions.

items.says: The evaluation-harness bullet does not state what decision or consequence followed detection of the two regressions.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether detection prevented a degraded release, changed checkpoint selection, or protected a user-facing metric.

items.says: The phrase "Wrote the evaluation harness" does not identify the technical capability that made the harness effective.
items.because: It shows ownership but gives limited evidence of what the harness automated or standardized.

items.says: The phrase "the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints" is indirect and adds filler.
items.because: It separates the harness from its purpose and delays the evaluation task.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking does not train the model to reproduce tool outputs more faithfully.
items.because: It excludes tool-output tokens from supervised loss and trains assistant responses conditioned on tool outputs instead.

items.says: The same adapter fine-tuning achievement is repeated on lines 9 and 13.
items.because: Both bullets describe the same domain adapter and assistant-only loss masking, making the second look duplicated.

items.says: The claim that BF16 mixed precision cut total GPU memory by 4x is likely overstated and ambiguous.
items.because: FP32 master weights and optimizer states can dominate memory, and "by 4x" does not clearly mean memory fell to one-quarter.

items.says: The load-test safeguard is appended after the main latency result and is easy to miss.
items.because: The build-gating condition is important proof that the target was enforced rather than observed only once.

items.says: The phrase "Maintained ... and adds" mixes past and present tense in a role that ended in July 2024.
items.because: The tense shift appears mechanically unedited and creates uncertainty about whether the checks were completed or ongoing.

items.says: The release-cycle result gives only a three-day endpoint and does not show the work beyond adding regression checks.
items.because: Readers cannot judge the acceleration without the prior cadence, and "Maintained" frames the work as routine responsibility.

items.says: The AI-first-practices bullet makes unsupported, broad causal claims without identifying the practices, adoption scale, or measured outcomes.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what was introduced, who adopted it, or whether delivery improved against a baseline.

items.says: The working-context claim does not identify the context being controlled or why the limit mattered, and the 100x growth lacks a baseline.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the limit prevented failures, reduced cost or latency, or enabled longer tasks.

items.says: The concurrency fix does not establish how extensively defects were removed, and "under 50-way fan-out" is compressed.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the defects were eliminated or whether failures occurred at or below 50 concurrent branches.

items.says: The evaluation-framework bullet does not state what capability or outcome integrating eight metrics enabled.
items.because: The count shows implementation scale but not improved coverage, reproducibility, or downstream value.

items.says: The phrase "Showed the evaluator tracks" is grammatically incomplete.
items.because: The missing conjunction makes the result read as an editing error.

items.says: The Kendall correlation supports a strong rank-order association, not the broader claim that the evaluator tracks degradation.
items.because: The statistic does not establish calibration, causal validity, human agreement, or generalization and lacks the reference ordering.

items.says: The résumé repeats the triage-branch achievement with inconsistent backlog figures.
items.because: The same result is reported as 68% in one place and two-thirds in another, making readers question which measurement is correct.

items.says: The phrase "ML-extracted" uses an unexplained abbreviation and makes the method less accessible.
items.because: Readers outside the immediate machine-learning context may not know that ML means machine learning.

items.says: The Research-Agent Evaluation Framework entry is weakened by a copied diagnostics bullet unrelated to its evaluation contribution.
items.because: The bullet switches to diagnostics triage and repeats the internship result, making the project look assembled from unrelated work.
